messages:
anya: Heads up — saw a spike of reconnects from EU clients, many with resume tokens that seem to be accepted against stale sticky leases. Console shows duplicate billing increments for some sessions. Anyone seen the LB strip or rewrite `x-sticky-lease` TTL?

matt: I pulled traces — nginx fronting the proxy returns 502 briefly, then downstream accepts a resume that claims lease=0. example from proxy logs:
```
[2026-03-22T21:14:03Z] client=10.2.3.4 resume_id=abc123 sticky_lease=0 route=shard-eu-01 accept=true
[2026-03-22T21:14:04Z] upstream=shard-eu-02 resume_id=abc123 sticky_lease=0 -> forwarded
```
Looks like header is present but TTL==0 and our routing still treats it as sticky.

josh: That explains duplicate billing. Our billing path counts a resumed stream as a continuing session even if lease expired. We should enforce resume idempotency + lease validation in the route gate. If lease==0 -> reject resume or mark not billable.

emily: Console metric `resume_dup_count` only fires on exact duplicate token matches; it's really noisy. Can we enrich telemetry with `lease_status` (stale|ok) and `route_shard` so ops can filter by region? Right now it's hard to tell if it's proxy rewrite vs client replay.

devex: Short term: return a 409 with body {"error":"resume_stale","info":"lease expired"} when we detect TTL expired. That avoids silently accepting and lets clients reconnect fresh. :thinking:

matt: Prefer a server-side conservative change: check header timestamp on resume path and if stale either 1) reject with 409 (safe) or 2) accept but tag request `resume_stale=true` and explicitly suppress billing. Option 2 is safer for rollouts but risks keeping odd sessions around.

anya: I lean to rejecting stale resumes (409) — that forces client to open a new session and keeps billing sane. We should also emit telemetry `resume_stale=true` with tags: `client_region`, `route_shard`, `proxy_upstream`. I'll open a rollout PR and a console annotation for the change.

josh: I'll add the metric + alert: fire if `resume_stale` > 0.5% of resumes in a 10m window for eu region. Also add a dashboard row mapping `resume_status` x `route_shard` so SRE can eyeball hotspots.

matt: Implementation note: in the resume handler patch we need to be careful to treat absent `x-sticky-lease` as "no-lease" not stale. Only reject when lease header present and TTL timestamp < now. Clients that don't send header should continue to be allowed to reconnect.

anya: Good call. Also add a short-lived console flag to turn the strict behavior off for canary tenants. I'll include a per-tenant rollout switch.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled for eng-platform/resume-lease-guard at 2026-03-22T22:00:00Z (canary 5% -> 50% -> 100%).

matt: I'll land the server-side guard and telemetry emit today. PR will include unit test for header parsing and an e2e that simulates nginx 502 + resume replay.

emily: I'll update the console to surface `resume_stale` and add the dashboard row. Also adding a note in the rollout UX: "Resume rejections will surface as 409 in streaming client logs."

anya: Thanks everyone. Action items: matt PR + tests, josh add metric & alert, emily dashboard + console flag, I'll open the rollout RFC with tenants to exclude during canary.

matt: ack :thumbsup:

josh: ack

ops-bot: incident-bot: no active incident linked to this thread.
